a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: L4 measured aqueous solubility for structurally related large pyrrolidine carbamate–imidazole HCV inhibitors is very low (parent PIB <0.1 mg/mL at pH 7.4, C52; phosphate prodrug 6.4 µg/mL, C51), and atazanavir, a comparably sized peptidomimetic carbamate, is <1 µg/mL at pH≥4 with only 30.56% pure-drug dissolution (C59, C54), supporting poor dissolution/absorption for this chemotype.

L5 identifies multiple HCV NS5A inhibitors of the same structural class (pibrentasvir, ledipasvir, ombitasvir, velpatasvir) as P-gp/BCRP substrates whose intestinal efflux can reduce oral exposure (C71, C69, C70, C66, C72), and P-gp inhibition increases exposure for repaglinide, rovatirelin, and sulpiride (C73, C63, C65), providing mechanistic evidence for presystemic loss in the query.

L1 high-F contexts (acalabrutinib 25.3%, AZD0837 22–55%, maraviroc 33%, asciminib ~73%) are direct but poorly transferable because the query is much larger (MW 738.9), more lipophilic (logP 6.22), and has higher TPSA (174.6) (C02, C01, C05, C10).

No direct F measurement for the query is available; the low prediction rests on coherent measured solubility and efflux liabilities in close analogs plus the unfavorable physicochemical prior, not on generic descriptors alone.
